title: Five books of prayers
hook: the Psalms are in five books, like the Torah, and cover every feeling

segments.voice: Yesterday, the last psalm, all trumpets and cymbals. Your line: your breath goes back as praise.

Open a Bible near the middle and you may well land in the Psalms: a hundred and fifty of them. For a month this path has walked through them: a tree by the water, a cry of my God, my God, a deer at a dry stream, a sparrow at the altar, a weaned child, exiles by the rivers of Babylon, and yesterday, a crash of cymbals. It can feel like a shuffle playlist: grief, then joy, then fury, then a lullaby. But it isn't a pile. Someone arranged it.
screen: `THE MIDDLE OF THE BIBLE.` → `A MONTH IN THE PSALMS.` → `NOT A PILE, A SHAPE.`

segments.voice: The Psalms are divided into five books. Book one runs from Psalm one to forty-one; book two, forty-two to seventy-two; book three, seventy-three to eighty-nine; book four, ninety to one hundred six; book five, one hundred seven to one hundred fifty. You can see the seams. The first four books each end with a blessing, like a door closing, and the fifth ends with yesterday's hallelujah. The first one, in the King James Bible: "Blessed be the LORD God of Israel from everlasting, and to everlasting. Amen, and Amen." At the end of book two there's a surprising little note: "The prayers of David the son of Jesse are ended." Except they aren't. More psalms of David come later. Some scholars think that line is left over from an older collection, a sign the book was gathered from earlier collections. An old Jewish commentary says that as Moses gave Israel five books of the law, David gave them five books of psalms. Inside, every feeling has a place. Lament runs all through it: complaint, grief, why, how long. Then praise, thanks, pilgrim songs, wisdom, songs for kings. Athanasius, a bishop of Alexandria, wrote that the other books of the Bible speak to you, but the Psalms speak for you; you find your own soul in them, as in a mirror. John Calvin later called the book an anatomy of all the parts of the soul. One more note: Greek and Latin Bibles number most psalms one lower, which is why Catholic and Orthodox prayer books can look off by one.
screen: `FIVE BOOKS, FIVE SEAMS` · `THE PRAYERS OF DAVID ARE ENDED` · `LAMENT RUNS ALL THROUGH IT` · `A MIRROR FOR THE SOUL` · then, large: `EVERY FEELING HAS A PSALM.`

segments.voice: Ask yourself honestly how you are, tired, grateful, angry, waiting, homesick, and let one of this month's psalms rise that fits: the deer at the dry stream, out of the depths, the weaned child, the new song. Pick the one that sounds like you, not the one you think you should, and if you pray, pray it.
Athanasius. The bishop of Alexandria who wrote that the Psalms speak for you, so that you find your own soul in them, as in a mirror.
Your line: every feeling has a psalm. The week ran from the depths to Hannah's weaned child, Babylon, being knit together, everything praising, and hallelujah. That's a whole book, done.

howItsDone: Many Christians pray through the whole book of Psalms regularly: monasteries traditionally chant all 150 every week, and the Book of Common Prayer sets them out to be read through every month.

chat.says: Is the book of Psalms just a random pile of old songs?
options: No, it's arranged in five books, each closing with a blessing or hallelujah.
Yes, they were bound in the order they were written, oldest first.
No, they're sorted by mood: all the sad ones first, then the happy ones.

notes: Week-end look-back (days 435–441) in the carry; the hook also looks back over the Psalms block (days 412–440).
'The longest book in the Bible' by chapter count (150). Confirm phrasing.
Midrash Tehillim 1:2: 'Moses gave Israel the five books of the Torah, and David gave Israel the five books of Psalms.' Paraphrased; confirm.

Athanasius, Letter to Marcellinus (ch. 10–12): the Psalms as a mirror; 'speak for you' is a paraphrase of his idea that the reader takes the psalms' words as their own. Confirm the paraphrase is fair.
Calvin's phrase 'an anatomy of all the parts of the soul' (preface to Commentary on the Psalms, 1557), paraphrased, not quoted. Confirm.
Lament as the largest category (Gunkel's form criticism; individual and communal laments together). Confirm.
howItsDone: Rule of St Benedict sets the full Psalter weekly; BCP 1662 monthly cycle. Confirm.
